problems.name: HumanEval_108_count_nums
problems.code:
def count_nums(arr)
    arr.count { |num| sum_of_digits(num) > 0 }
end

def sum_of_digits(num)
    digits = num.to_s.chars.map(&:to_i)
    if num < 0
        digits[0] *= -1
    end
    digits.sum
end

require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_count_nums
    candidate = method(:count_nums)
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call([]))
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call([-1, -2, 0]))
    assert_equal(6, candidate.call([1, 1, 2, -2, 3, 4, 5]))
    assert_equal(5, candidate.call([1, 6, 9, -6, 0, 1, 5]))
    assert_equal(4, candidate.call([1, 100, 98, -7, 1, -1]))
    assert_equal(5, candidate.call([12, 23, 34, -45, -56, 0]))
    assert_equal(1, candidate.call([0, 1]))
    assert_equal(1, candidate.call([1]))
  end
end

problems.name: HumanEval_111_histogram
problems.code:
def histogram(test)
  return {} if test.empty?
  
  letters = test.split(' ')
  counts = Hash.new(0)
  
  letters.each { |letter| counts[letter] += 1 }
  
  max_count = counts.values.max
  counts.select { |_, count| count == max_count }
end

require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_histogram
    candidate = method(:histogram)
    assert_equal({"a" => 2, "b" => 2}, candidate.call("a b b a"))
    assert_equal({"a" => 2, "b" => 2}, candidate.call("a b c a b"))
    assert_equal({"a" => 1, "b" => 1, "c" => 1, "d" => 1, "g" => 1}, candidate.call("a b c d g"))
    assert_equal({"r" => 1, "t" => 1, "g" => 1}, candidate.call("r t g"))
    assert_equal({"b" => 4}, candidate.call("b b b b a"))
    assert_equal({"r" => 1, "t" => 1, "g" => 1}, candidate.call("r t g"))
    assert_equal({}, candidate.call(""))
    assert_equal({"a" => 1}, candidate.call("a"))
  end
end

# >>> filter_by_prefix.call([], "a")

problems.name: HumanEval_103_rounded_avg
problems.code:
def rounded_avg(n, m)
    return -1 if n > m
    
    sum = (n..m).sum
    count = m - n + 1
    average = (sum.to_f / count).round
    
    "0b#{average.to_s(2)}"
end

    assert_equal("0b1001110010", candidate.call(350, 902))

    assert_equal(-1, candidate.call(7, 5))
    assert_equal(-1, candidate.call(5, 1))

def specialFilter(nums)
    count = 0
    nums.each do |num|
        if num > 10 && odd?(num.to_s[0].to_i) && odd?(num.to_s[-1].to_i)
            count += 1
        end
    end
    count
end

def odd?(n)
    n % 2 == 1
end

problems.name: HumanEval_87_get_row
problems.code:
# You are given a 2 dimensional data, as a nested arrays,
# which is similar to matrix, however, unlike matrices,
# each row may contain a different number of columns.
# Given lst, and integer x, find integers x in the array,
# and return array of arrays, [(x1, y1), (x2, y2) ...] such that
# each array is a coordinate - (row, columns), starting with 0.
# Sort coordinates initially by rows in ascending order.
# Also, sort coordinates of the row by columns in descending order.
# Examples:
# >>> get_row.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1]], 1)
# [[0, 0], [1, 4], [1, 0], [2, 5], [2, 0]]
# >>> get_row.call([], 1)
# []
# >>> get_row.call([[], [1], [1, 2, 3]], 3)
# [[2, 2]]
def get_row(lst, x)
coordinates = []

    lst.each_with_index do |row, row_index|
        row.each_with_index do |value, col_index|
            if value == x
                coordinates << [row_index, col_index]
            end
        end
    end

    # Sort by rows ascending, then by columns descending within each row
    coordinates.sort_by { |row, col| [row, -col] }
end
end


require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_get_row
    candidate = method(:get_row)
    assert_equal([[0, 0], [1, 4], [1, 0], [2, 5], [2, 0]], candidate.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1]], 1))
    assert_equal([[0, 1], [1, 1], [2, 1], [3, 1], [4, 1], [5, 1]], candidate.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]], 2))
    assert_equal([[0, 0], [1, 0], [2, 1], [2, 0], [3, 2], [3, 0], [4, 3], [4, 0], [5, 4], [5, 0], [6, 5], [6, 0]], candidate.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 1, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 1, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1]], 1))
    assert_equal([], candidate.call([], 1))
    assert_equal([], candidate.call([[1]], 2))
    assert_equal([[2, 2]], candidate.call([[], [1], [1, 2, 3]], 3))
  end
end

problems.name: HumanEval_69_search
problems.code:
def search(lst)
    freq = Hash.new(0)
    lst.each { |num| freq[num] += 1 }
    
    max_num = -1
    
    freq.each do |num, count|
        if num <= count && num > max_num
            max_num = num
        end
    end
    
    max_num
end

problems.name: HumanEval_131_digits
problems.code:
def digits(n)
    product = 1
    has_odd = false
    
    while n > 0
        digit = n % 10
        if digit.odd?
            product *= digit
            has_odd = true
        end
        n /= 10
    end
    
    has_odd ? product : 0
end

require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_digits

    assert_equal(5, candidate.call(54))

    assert_equal(5, candidate.call(5014))
    assert_equal(315, candidate.call(98765))
    assert_equal(2625, candidate.call(5576543))
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call(2468))
  end
end
